section: Major Harappan sites and their signature finds - Harappa, Mohenjodaro, Chanhudaro, Lothal, Dholavira, Kalibangan, Banawali, Rakhigarhi, Surkotada, Rangpur

accepted.s: The Pashupati seal, depicting a three-faced figure in yogic posture surrounded by animals, was discovered at which Harappan site?
accepted.x: The Pashupati seal, also called the Proto-Shiva seal, was found at Mohenjodaro. It depicts a three-faced figure in a yogic posture, surrounded by animals.
accepted.tq: Use the site-specific association directly; distinguish Mohenjodaro from other major urban sites.

accepted.s: The Bronze Dancing Girl of the Harappan civilisation was found at
accepted.x: The Bronze Dancing Girl is one of the best-known sculptures discovered at Mohenjodaro.
accepted.tq: Test a famous object–site association through direct recall.

accepted.s: The famous steatite statue known as the Priest-King was discovered at
accepted.x: The bearded steatite figure known as the Priest-King was found at Mohenjodaro.
accepted.tq: Separate closely related Mohenjodaro sculptures by their identifying material and title.

accepted.s:
Consider the following statements regarding finds from Harappa:
1. A red sandstone male torso was found there.
2. A bronze dog chasing a deer was found there.
3. Bullock carts have been associated with the site.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
accepted.x: All three statements are correct. Harappa has yielded a red sandstone male torso, a bronze dog chasing a deer, and bullock carts.
accepted.tq: Check whether all objects in a site-specific cluster belong to the same site.

accepted.s: Which one of the following pairs is correctly matched?
o: Chanhudaro — carts with seated drivers and toy objects
accepted.x: Carts with seated drivers and toy objects were found at Chanhudaro. The Bronze Dancing Girl, Pashupati seal and Priest-King are associated with Mohenjodaro, while the listed Harappa and Kalibangan associations are incorrect.
accepted.tq: Start from the sure site–find pair and eliminate swapped objects from neighbouring sites.

accepted.s:
Which of the following finds is associated with Lothal?
1. A ship depicted on a seal
2. A Persian Gulf seal
3. A copper dog
Select the correct answer using the code given below.
accepted.x: All three finds—a ship on a seal, a Persian Gulf seal and a copper dog—are associated with Lothal.
accepted.tq: Use a complete site-specific list and test whether any item has been wrongly transferred to another site.

accepted.s: With reference to cylindrical seals in the Harappan context, which one of the following is correct?
o: They were found only at Lothal and Dholavira.
They were found exclusively at Chanhudaro.
They were found only at Harappa.
They were found at Kalibangan, while a Mesopotamian-linked cylindrical seal was found at Mohenjodaro.
accepted.x: Cylindrical seals are associated with Kalibangan, and a cylindrical seal indicating a Mesopotamian link was found at Mohenjodaro.
accepted.tq: Distinguish a general site association from the specific Mesopotamian-linked find.

accepted.s: Which one of the following statements regarding Harappan seal motifs and plant representation is correct?
o: The rhinoceros is the most common seal motif and the acacia is the most depicted tree.
The unicorn is the most common seal motif and the pipal is the most depicted tree.
The elephant is the most common seal motif and the banyan is the most depicted tree.
The bull is the most common seal motif and the neem is the most depicted tree.
accepted.x: The unicorn is regarded as the most common Harappan seal motif, while the pipal is the most depicted tree.
accepted.tq: Test a paired comparison by separating the most common motif from the most depicted tree.

accepted.s: The skeletons from Rakhigarhi were transferred under a Memorandum of Understanding to which institution?
o: Archaeological Survey of India, New Delhi
Indian Council of Historical Research, New Delhi
accepted.x: The Rakhigarhi skeletons were transferred by the Archaeological Survey of India to the Anthropological Survey of India at Kolkata under an MoU.
accepted.tq: Identify the correct institution and location rather than confusing neighbouring heritage bodies.

accepted.s:
Consider the following statements about Mound 7 at Rakhigarhi:
1. It has yielded 56 skeletons in all.
2. The assemblage includes a woman estimated to be about 4,600 years old.
3. The skeletons were transferred to the Anthropological Survey of India at Kolkata under an MoU.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
accepted.x: All three statements are correct. Mound 7 yielded 56 skeletons, including a woman approximately 4,600 years old, and the skeletons were transferred to the Anthropological Survey of India, Kolkata, under an MoU.
accepted.tq: Combine numerical, chronological and institutional details while checking every statement independently.

accepted.s: The latest reported excavation at Rakhigarhi yielded which of the following?
o: Three complete skeletons aged 20–30 years and five fragmentary burials
Five complete skeletons aged 30–40 years and three fragmentary burials
Eight complete skeletons, all belonging to women
Five complete skeletons aged 40–50 years and two fragmentary burials
accepted.x: The latest reported excavation yielded five complete skeletons of individuals aged about 30–40 years and three fragmentary burials.
accepted.tq: Compare both the count and age range; numerical distractors alter one detail of the true finding.

accepted.s: Which one of the following correctly compares the building materials used at the Harappan sites?
o: Dholavira used baked brick, whereas Mohenjodaro and Harappa used sandstone and limestone.
All three sites used only baked brick.
All three sites used only limestone.
Dholavira used sandstone and limestone, whereas Mohenjodaro and Harappa used baked brick.
accepted.x: Dholavira used sandstone and limestone, while Mohenjodaro and Harappa used baked brick.
accepted.tq: Watch for the reversed-comparison trap in which the materials of two site groups are interchanged.

accepted.s:
Arrange the following objects according to their associated Harappan sites from the site-specific associations given below:
A. Pashupati seal
B. Ship on a seal
C. Carts with seated drivers
D. Red sandstone male torso
Which one of the following correctly identifies the sites in the same order?
accepted.x: The Pashupati seal is from Mohenjodaro, the ship on a seal from Lothal, carts with seated drivers from Chanhudaro, and the red sandstone male torso from Harappa.
accepted.tq: Use a sure first pair and then map the remaining objects by site association.
